title: Universal open containment locus for a finite locally free family
statement: Let $p:E\to B$ be a finite locally free morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $Y\hookrightarrow E$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $p(|E|\setminus|Y|)$ is closed in $B$, and the open subscheme $O_Y=B\setminus p(|E|\setminus|Y|)$ has the following property: a morphism of schemes $a:T\to B$ factors (necessarily uniquely) through $O_Y$ if and only if the projection $E\times_BT\to E$ [def-pc-fibre-product] factors through $Y$. This locus commutes with arbitrary base change on $B$. The rank may vary or be zero.

source.place: BLR 7.6 Proposition 2(ii), printed pp.192–194 (PDF pp.198–200), finite locally free case: the open scheme representing whole-family containment in an open subscheme. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Write $j:Y\hookrightarrow E$ and $C=|E|\setminus j(|Y|)$. The open-immersion definition makes $j(|Y|)$ open, hence $C$ closed. By the finite-locally-free definition $p$ is finite. Apply the closed-map clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] to $C$: $p(C)$ is closed. Thus its complement defines the open subscheme $O_Y$ of $B$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), together with the open-subscheme construction of schemes.tex, Tag 01HH (lemma-open-immersion); BLR 7.6 Proposition 2(i) uses this closed image.

proof.text: For an open immersion $i:V\hookrightarrow X$ and any $h:Z\to X$, a factorization of $h$ through $i$ exists exactly when $h(|Z|)\subseteq i(|V|)$, and is then unique. Indeed by [def-weil-open-immersion] $i$ induces an isomorphism $V\cong(U,\mathcal O_X|_U)$ onto the open subscheme on $U=i(|V|)$, compatible with the inclusion $j_U$. If $h(|Z|)\subseteq U$, [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] gives a unique $h':Z\to U$ with $j_U\circ h'=h$; composing $h'$ with $U\cong V$ gives a lift through $i$, and any lift through $i$ composed with $V\cong U$ is a lift through $j_U$, hence equals $h'$ by that uniqueness. Conversely a lift $g$ with $i\circ g=h$ forces $h(|Z|)=i(g(|Z|))\subseteq i(|V|)$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01HH (lemma-open-immersion) and the open-subscheme restriction preceding it; Mathlib IsOpenImmersion.lift / lift_fac / lift_uniq (OpenImmersion.lean:701-708).

proof.text: Let $a:T\to B$, $P=E\times_BT$, and let $r:P\to E$, $q:P\to T$ be the projections of [def-pc-fibre-product]. The arbitrary-subset formula in [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image], with $f=p$, $g=a$ and subset $C$, gives $q(r^{-1}(C))=a^{-1}(p(C))$. Thus $r^{-1}(C)=\varnothing$ if and only if $a^{-1}(p(C))=\varnothing$: a set has empty image exactly when it is empty. These are respectively $r(|P|)\subseteq j(|Y|)$ and $a(|T|)\subseteq |O_Y|$. Apply step 2 to $j$ and $O_Y\hookrightarrow B$ to obtain exactly the claimed equivalence and uniqueness.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01S1 (lemma-base-change-surjective), proof: image/preimage identity for an arbitrary subset, using Tag 0495 (lemma-when-point-maps-to-pair).

proof.text: For any $b:B^{\prime}\to B$, put $E^{\prime}=E\times_BB^{\prime}$ with projections $r^{\prime},p^{\prime}$ and $Y^{\prime}=Y\times_BB^{\prime}$. The open restriction of $E^{\prime}$ to $(r^{\prime})^{-1}(j(|Y|))$ is $Y^{\prime}$: a map into that restriction is a map into $E^{\prime}$ whose composite into $E$ lifts to $Y$ by step 2, which is precisely a map into the displayed fibre product. Consequently its complement is $C^{\prime}=(r^{\prime})^{-1}(C)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image] again to obtain $p^{\prime}(C^{\prime})=b^{-1}(p(C))$. This is closed by continuity of $b$, and taking complements gives $|O_{Y^{\prime}}|=b^{-1}(|O_Y|)$. The same restriction and fibre-product argument identifies the corresponding open subschemes: $O_{Y^{\prime}}\cong O_Y\times_BB^{\prime}$ over $B^{\prime}$. Nothing used a positive or constant rank. In particular if $E$ is empty then $C=\varnothing$, $O_Y=B$, and both factorization conditions always hold.

Step 1: def-pc-finite-locally-free gives finite, and clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres (Mathlib Scheme.Hom.isClosedMap, UniversallyClosed.lean:49) makes p(C) closed for the closed set C = |E| minus j(|Y|). Steps 3 and 4: lem-weil-pbc-base-change-image (image_preimage_eq_of_isPullback, PullbackCarrier.lean:420, any subset, any pullback square) gives q(r^{-1}C) = a^{-1}(pC) and p'(C') = b^{-1}(pC). From these, a:T->B factors through O_Y exactly when E x_B T -> E factors through Y, and the locus is stable under any base change b, with no flatness assumption on b. Edge cases tested: E empty, Y empty over Spec k, the finite non-flat closed point of A^1, a nonreduced base. All agree, so the statement is true. No duplicate node for this locus exists in the DAG, and the off-unit citations are all Mathlib leaves, so no tool_uses are needed.
